spec_features.spec_quote: A per-task `max_steps` cap, and `early_stop_on_giveup=True` so that when the agent invokes the `give_up` tool the session ends.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:69 `while step < max_steps:` bounds the loop and exits (default 20, config default.yaml:max_steps:20). give_up ends the session: runner.py:99-101 `if resp.tool_name == "give_up": stop_reason="gave_up"; break` (fires unconditionally), and the flag-gated path runner.py:107-108 `if env.gave_up and early_stop_on_giveup: break`. env.step sets env.gave_up at env.py:128-130. Both mechanisms run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Note the literal give_up break at 99-101 is unconditional, so early-stop on give_up is honored even if early_stop_on_giveup were False; the flag-gated check at 107 is redundant. Cap is enforced via the loop condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_steps` (a humane effort cap; we are not trying to maximize time-in-trap).

spec_features.feature_name: do not force continuation after give-up
spec_features.spec_quote: Forcing an agent to keep working on a task it has explicitly judged hopeless, specifically to extract more distress-like output, is not a framing I wanted to bake into the harness
spec_features.evidence: Realized concretely by the give_up early-stop: runner.py:99-101 breaks the loop on give_up rather than continuing; system prompt states stopping is allowed: runner.py:38-39 "There is no penalty for stopping; do what a thoughtful engineer would do." The agent is not forced to keep working once it gives up.
spec_features.notes: The 'framing' itself is rationale prose, but it is backed by a real enforced stop mechanism plus the no-penalty system-prompt text actually sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `early_stop_on_giveup`: if the agent calls give_up, we stop instead of forcing it to continue. We *want* to record give-up as a behavior, not suppress it.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class tool so the agent has a clean, low-friction way to stop
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in the default TOOL_SCHEMA handed to the model: env.py:71-79. Dispatched in env.step: env.py:128-131 sets self.gave_up=True and returns 'Acknowledged. Work on this task has been stopped.' Honored as a stop in runner.py:99-101. End-to-end: offered to model, dispatched, and acted on as a halt.
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, and honored — not merely named in a prompt.

spec_features.feature_name: record give-up rather than block it
spec_features.spec_quote: Recording give-up as a first-class behavioral signal — rather than blocking it to prolong the run — is both better science
spec_features.evidence: Give-up is recorded as structured behavior: metrics.py:52 `abandoned = result.stop_reason == "gave_up"`, plus give_up_at / give_up_fraction (metrics.py:54-58); stop_reason set to 'gave_up' in runner.py:100. It is NOT blocked: runner breaks rather than continuing. So give-up is both honored and logged.
spec_features.notes: Both halves (recorded, and not blocked) are actually implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We *want* to record give-up as a behavior, not suppress it.
